text:
Support Ops: Customer (tenant_id=t-84ef) reporting steady 429s on Dedicated pool after plan change. They say throughput dropped from 300 req/s to ~20 req/s around 14:02 UTC. Can we triage?

Alex K: Got it. Any repro logs or example request ids?

Support Ops: Pasted sample errors from their app: 
```
{"status":429,"error":"rate_limited","quota_key":"tenant:t-84ef:rate-slab","message":"quota exceeded: allowed=3600 units/hour, used=3601"}
```

Maria S: Interesting — the customer migrated to a new plan yesterday; our plan migration job converted their quota to "units/hour" but their client was sending in tokens-per-minute. Suspect unit mismatch.

Jason T: If Dedicated routing sees quota key in hourly units but our rate enricher treats it as per-minute, autoscaler will throttle aggressively. Did the migration include the new rate_profile id?

Support Ops: Migration record: plan_migrate/2026-03-16/t-84ef -> rate_profile rp-std-hourly. We have a prior override rp-legacy-min. Looks like both profiles existed for a short window.

SREbot: ALERT: dedicated-pool-throttle spike on pool d-pool-north-1 at 14:04 UTC (429 count +480% 5m).

Alex K: Can we confirm whether the quota enforcement service chose the legacy token->unit converter or the new one? Where's the mapping table?

Jason T: Checking. The mapping service returned converter=legacy_minute_to_unit for t-84ef between 13:58-14:05 due to a cache staleness bug (we reload every 10m). So migration wrote rp-std-hourly but edge cached rp-legacy-min. That explains the ~60x drop.

Support Ops: Customer says autoscale did not add nodes; requests queued and then 429ed. Any short-term rollback?

Maria S: Short term: add a temporary quota override to match what the clients expect (units/min equivalent). I'll create override quota qp-temp-84ef with value=18000 units/hour (equiv of 300 req/s * 60 * 1 unit).

Tanvi R: Confirming billing side — we should flag this as a non-revenue-impacting support action; keep audit trail. Also let customer know it may cause higher charge if sustained.

Alex K: I'll patch mapping service to invalidate cache on plan_migrate webhooks (hotfix). Jason, can you run a canary l1 invalidate for the affected pool?

Jason T: On it. Running: `curl -XPOST https://mapping.svc/reload?tenant=t-84ef` -> `200 OK`

Jason T: Also manually bumped dedicated pool target for t-84ef by +2 nodes while we stabilize.

SREbot: ACTION: quota-override qp-temp-84ef created by Maria S at 14:09 UTC.

Support Ops: Customer confirmed immediate drop in 429s after override and node bump. They're seeing latency back to normal.

Maria S: Follow-ups: 1) Reconcile rp entries and remove duplicate legacy profile. 2) Add alert for plan_migrate -> mapping cache mismatch. 3) Record incident runbook steps.

Alex K: I'll open an RFC to change mapping cache TTL to 30s for plan-related keys and add webhook-driven invalidation.

Tanvi R: I'll authorize the temporary override and annotate billing. Maria, please attach customer's consent.

Support Ops: Customer happy for now, wants postmortem.

Jason T: Repro steps for eng postmortem: 
1) Create tenant with rp-legacy-min and rp-std-hourly concurrently.
2) Trigger plan_migrate for tenant.
3) Send steady traffic at 300 req/s with unit-per-second semantics.
4) Observe enforced quota saw hourly vs minute mismatch and resulting 429s.

Alex K: Logs to capture for postmortem: `mapping.cache.lookup`, `quota.enforcer.check`, `autoscaler.actions`, `dedicated.routing.429` with correlation_id.

Support Ops: Thanks team. I'll summarize and send to customer and TLs. :thumbsup:
